summary: A 62-foot (19 m) concrete-and-steel lighthouse finished in 2010 on Clover Island in the Columbia River at Kennewick, Washington. A private aid to navigation.

access.note: A plaza of about 3,700 square feet surrounds the tower; a causeway reaches the island from North Washington Street in Kennewick. Rowlett's directory says 'Site open, tower closed.' The U.S. Lighthouse Society archive marks the site 'Open to Public: No'.

events.note: Constructed May 2010 (Port of Kennewick). The Associated Press reported on 7 January 2010 that it would start functioning the next month.

corrections.why: 19.0 m is the tower's height (62 ft). Rowlett's directory gives a focal plane of about 70 ft (21 m). The USCG Light List (navcen.uscg.gov, blocked to this agent with HTTP 403) could not be checked to confirm either figure.

notes_for_editor: Thin station: no keepers, no wrecks, no storms; the history is the 2010 build and its current status. Disagreements: (1) Completion date: the AP (7 Jan 2010) expected it to function the next month; the Port gives May 2010 as the construction date, and Rowlett gives September 2009 to May 2010. The story says the sources do not agree. (2) Status: the Port calls it a Coast Guard-approved private aid to navigation (ARLHS agrees: 'Private aid'); the DCI project page calls it a 'U.S. Coast Guard lighthouse'; the USLHS record calls it a 'Minor Aid to Navigation'. (3) Height and focal plane: the record's focal_height_m 19.0 is the tower height; Rowlett gives a focal plane of about 70 ft (21 m); ARLHS describes a 35-foot black and tan conical tower, which matches none of the other sources (see corrections). (4) Access: Rowlett says 'Site open, tower closed'; the USLHS record says 'Open to Public: No'; the Port describes a public plaza and causeway. The tower is recorded as closed; whether its interior can be entered is not stated. Human check recommended. (5) Construction: the Port says four pre-cast sections; Mountain States (August 2010) says the panels were poured on site, and DCI's blog describes on-site casting in wood forms with tilt-up construction; the story gives both. (6) Builder and owner: Mountain States names the Port as owner and itself as contractor; the story does not say the Port built it with its own crews. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the Mountain States PDF is dated August 2010 (source title corrected from 'undated'). Not verified against primary records: the USCG Light List (navcen.uscg.gov, HTTP 403 to this agent) and the USCG Aids to Navigation Team Kennewick fact sheet (pacificarea.uscg.mil, HTTP 403). Wikipedia says the USCG Aids to Navigation Team Kennewick is headquartered on Clover Island; that fact was left out because the fact sheet it leads to could not be read. Wikipedia used for leads only. Newspaper and corpus checks: corpus.py grep 'Clover Island' (WA) found nothing (the light dates from 2010, after the corpus's periods). Chronicling America not searched: the light postdates its coverage. Retry for fuller coverage: the Tri-City Herald (Jan 2010) and Wenatchee World reprint timed out or returned HTTP 429 to this agent; the LOC photo record 2018698971 returned 403. Position: the record's OSM point 46.217763, -119.116227 matches ARLHS (46.21766, -119.11620); the USLHS place record (-119.1067) and the Wikipedia infobox (-119.1111) differ by under 1 km; no correction proposed. The Wikipedia lead says Lewis and Clark visited the island on 17 Oct 1805; the USGS page read here names Clover Island only in its menu and does not confirm the visit, so the story leaves it out. Photos: the record's Wikimedia Commons photo was not reviewed; none new.
